Create one exceptionally polished full desktop game-client concept image for STARNET, an autonomous AI workforce physically operating inside an explorable station. This is a visual theme of an existing application, preserving its physical-station metaphor. Use the attached StarNet OSRS concept as the strict COMPOSITION and DETAIL benchmark: elevated orthographic/isometric cutaway station, recognizable human-sized NPCs, visible functional equipment, left navigation, circular top-right minimap, right station/mission/crew panel, and bottom-left activity/chat. Keep the same proportions: left navigation about 13% width, right instrument rail about 24%, a generous central world dominating the remaining area, compact branded header, chat below the world. Output a single landscape 3:2 screen at 4K with no laptop, phone, browser chrome, collage, inset views, advertising copy or photographic surroundings.
Create entirely new art for the requested theme: different architecture, real material textures, role-specific outfits, equipment silhouettes, frame design, light and atmosphere. Match the reference's richness of modeled geometry, believable soft contact shadows, hand-authored material wear, disciplined perspective and small readable NPC proportions. Render full detailed characters, never stick figures, dots or generic geometric pawns. Avoid a flat recolour of the source. Avoid empty corporate-dashboard layouts, floating SaaS cards and excessive bloom. The central world must be a coherent inhabited playable space with clear walking routes and depth ordering; equipment stands on the floor and NPCs visibly face or use it.
Retain the STARNET gold compass/star emblem and legible STARNET wordmark at top-left, tagline "AUTONOMOUS WORK. REAL RESULTS.", an understated "Pacisia Online" status, and a compact UI STYLE control bearing the requested theme name. Left navigation: Station, Agents, Missions, Projects, Files, Integrations, Analytics, Settings. Replace each navigation icon with beautifully rendered small icons matching this theme.
Show nine distinct entities: Operator (central commander), Research Agent (rear-left research terminal), Analytics Agent (rear-centre data console), Content Agent (rear-right media workstation), Security Agent (right side), Data Agent (left craft/data bench), Finance Agent (front-left resource counter), Integration Agent (front-right relay), Build Agent (front-right engineering bench). No RuneScape NPC names or armour remain in these NEW themes. Preserve the OSRS version separately. Labels are discreet pale gold actual ROLE names with readable light text; avoid labels obscuring faces. Some NPCs work, some walk and the operator stands centrally. Furnish the room with a web/communications antenna, file archive cabinet, coding/terminal workbench, research desk, server stack, analytics console, image/media studio, integration relay, persistent storage and central mission table, all clearly distinguishable and grounded in the theme.
The circular minimap accurately depicts THIS room's footprint, the visible equipment and all nine crew positions, with a small compass and neat task markers; it is not a stock map. The right panel has Station Overview, Current Mission and Active Agents with miniature portraits matching the world NPCs. Use restrained example values: "9 / 9" agents, "3" active tasks, mission "Research suppliers", plus compact crew status phrases. The bottom chat uses carefully aligned timestamps and readable short lines: "[17:18] StarNet: Welcome to your station.", "[17:19] Research: Reviewing suppliers.", "[17:19] Build: Updating comparison sheet.", "[17:20] Analytics: Comparing margins.". Preserve a usable command entry and compact relevant channel tabs. These are visual concept examples, not proof of a live provider task. Maintain excellent visual readability at desktop size and precise crisp text.
THEME ART DIRECTION:
SPACE COLONY. A premium, convincingly modeled isometric orbital habitat in the spirit of a detailed industrial space-colony simulation. Octagonal room with chunky off-white painted hull walls, graphite steel floor plates, exposed bolts, scuffed orange safety strips, recessed airlocks and a huge curved rear observation window showing a blue planet in space. The room feels engineered, warm and lived in. A clean dark gunmetal game-client frame with fine warm ivory typography, muted orange/amber highlights, tactile metal buttons and an orange navigation selection. The room is well-lit by soft neutral task lighting and daylight from the planet; high quality shadows give every piece of equipment weight. Distinct human crew in chunky detailed astronaut workwear: white/gold commander, teal research scientist with tablet, navy analytics technician, purple media specialist, armoured charcoal security guard, orange utility crafter, dark executive finance uniform, green communications technician, ochre engineer with tools. Believable helmets or open-face suits according to role, clearly visible faces and hands, varied figures. Cyber equipment is rugged, functional and richly detailed: dish mounted on a swivel base, rack servers with tiny blue status lights, stacked storage lockers, dual-monitor desks, exposed engineering tools, wiring and a central tactical table with a subtle blue planet projection. Two small hydroponic planters soften the machinery. Interface icons use sculpted miniature equipment. Strong silhouette clarity, restrained cyan glow and a tactile finished game-client look.

THEME ART DIRECTION:
CYBERPUNK WORKSHOP. A dense, cinematic but readable orbital maintenance workshop in a neon city district. Replace medieval stone with layered dark graphite hull panels, ribbed steel trim, concrete composite floor tiles, industrial cable trays, exposed pipes, welded seams and subtle grime. A rear observation window reveals distant towers, wet glass and a vivid magenta/cyan city atmosphere, while the station interior stays sharply readable and has no rain on the floor. Use rich midnight navy rather than dull brown; cyan edge lighting, small magenta accents and the StarNet amber insignia. The room's lighting comes from credible console screens and overhead strips, with beautiful controlled shadows and no giant nebulous bloom. NPCs are detailed small isometric retro-3D people with clean faceted silhouettes and material texture: amber-visored operator in white jacket, research scientist in ivory/teal coat, silver-haired analyst in violet technical suit holding a tablet, content creator in a purple long coat, security in dark full tactical armour with cyan visor, data worker in orange utility clothes, financier in black/gold formal coat, integration tech in green fibre-optic jacket, build engineer with yellow tool belt and cybernetic forearm. No featureless stick characters. Equipment includes cable-heavy multimonitor terminals, a tough archive locker, phased-array communications dish, a media recording rig, compact server stack, a tool-covered bench and a cyan/magenta holographic mission table. The surrounding game client uses beautifully finished black metal frames, precise hairline cyan trims, tactile illuminated tabs, compact monospaced telemetry paired with clean readable labels, and a dark chat surface with restrained semantic message colours. Avoid generic purple rectangular dashboard cards. Ensure all panels, minimap and portraits are rendered with the same finish as the world.

THEME ART DIRECTION:
STARSHIP BRIDGE. A refined retro-futurist command deck of a sophisticated deep-space vessel, with a broad wraparound rear viewport showing a star field and a distant pale planet. Warm ivory structural panels, midnight navy recessed walls, muted burgundy seats, brushed silver framework, dark slate polygon floor, graceful curved rails and consoles arranged around a central mission table. Controlled clean architecture with substantial, fully modeled equipment and authentic game-world depth, not a sterile flat wireframe. A few amber physical switches and soft blue-green instrument screens retain StarNet's gold/amber identity. Cinematic yet practical lighting, detailed soft shadows and elegantly restrained emissive screens. Nine finely rendered low-poly human crew in smart tailored uniforms with role-coded trim: gold operator commander, teal research scientist, navy/silver analytics officer, purple content/communications producer, burgundy security officer with plated shoulder guards, rust/orange data quartermaster, charcoal/gold finance administrator, green integration officer, ochre engineering officer with technical tools. Unique head shapes, hair and faces distinguish them. Equipment remains discrete physical tools: communications antenna behind the hull, a wall data archive, open coding workstation, analytics tactical console, media desk, server cabinet and engineering service bench. In the UI use navy enamel and brushed-metal framing, ivory text, small gold star insignia, crisp readable sci-fi typography and beautifully sculpted miniature role icons. The circular minimap is a precise clean bridge sensor with real matching room layout, tiny crew markers and fine compass; side panel and chat are understated shipboard interfaces with visible depth and material finish. Make the bridge warm, elegant, inhabited and explorable.

THEME ART DIRECTION:
STEAMPUNK AIRSHIP. A lavishly detailed command workshop aboard a steam-powered airship sailing through a starry sky. Octagonal cutaway room with rich aged timber floorboards, dark iron structural ribs, riveted brass wall cladding, copper pipes, pressure valves and curved portholes revealing a distant moon and clouds. Refined Victorian industrial craft rather than cluttered fantasy chaos. Warm amber task lamps, a restrained teal glow from analytical lenses, rich tactile wood grain, oxidized brass highlights and believable soft shadows. Put readable walking paths between substantial desks and machinery. Characters are charming but serious detailed isometric low-poly Victorian specialists: captain/operator in a navy coat with gold trim, research scholar in a teal waistcoat carrying books, elder analyst with spectacles and parchment, purple-coated artist/content agent, iron-and-brass armoured guard, aproned data crafter, banker in a plum suit, green-coated communications technician, stocky engineer with leather apron, wrench and brass goggles. Equipment expresses the same real capabilities: a rotating brass communications dish, a mahogany archive cabinet, a mechanical coding/typewriter bench with tiny cathode display, research desk with books and glass instruments, stacked brass compute engines, analytics dials, media engraving/recording desk, relay coils and a central celestial mission table. The surrounding game client uses beautifully modeled dark timber and worn brass frames, cream engraved type, parchment chat with brown ink and role colour accents, amber selection state and richly rendered tool icons. The circular minimap resembles a brass navigational instrument with etched compass and correctly matching room/crew markers. Preserve the main composition while making the machinery, outfit choices and airship architecture original and distinctive.

THEME ART DIRECTION:
SECRET-AGENT HQ. A cinematic mid-century espionage command bunker aboard a covert orbital outpost. Octagonal cutaway room with olive-grey concrete composite walls, charcoal floor, dark walnut desk surfaces, brushed steel archive cabinets, red leather chairs, restrained green terminal screens and an amber StarNet insignia. A rear shuttered observation window shows a night-side planet and surveillance satellites. Mood is sophisticated, practical and covert, not black-on-black: warm downlights keep people and equipment clearly readable. Beautiful fine material wear, fully modeled small machinery, strong contact shadows and discreet details such as reel-to-reel tape, rotary hardware, a locked equipment locker and classified folders. Nine detailed isometric human operatives with instantly different roles: central field commander in cream shirt and charcoal trousers, research investigator in tan coat with notebook, older analyst with spectacles and navy sweater, content/media specialist in burgundy suit at a recording desk, security guard in dark full tactical armour, data technician in olive workwear, finance controller in pinstripe suit, communications specialist in green jacket and headset, build engineer in grey mechanic overalls carrying tools. Keep skin, hair and hands visible and differentiated; no stick figures. Each capability is physical: intercept antenna, file cabinets, multimonitor intelligence desk, coding workbench, reel-based server equipment, analytics plotting console, media studio and a central illuminated mission map table. The game-client frame is dark walnut, gunmetal and enamel, compact professional lettering with amber headings, believable button depth and precisely rendered miniature folder/tool/crew icons. The circular minimap is a readable radar instrument matching this bunker, with thin green sweep graphics and actual marker positions. Chat is an elegant dark communications log with legible type, a command line and restrained message colours. Make this an inhabited playable headquarters with a finished premium game-client appearance.
